title: Multi-language SDK release pipeline: reproducible artifacts, signing, and ergonomic streaming retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a single, auditable release pipeline that publishes Python, TypeScript (npm), and Go SDK artifacts with reproducible provenance and artifact signing. This ticket ties release engineering work to recent SDK changes that introduce streaming ergonomics and a unified retry contract across languages. Goals:
- Implement CI workflows that produce reproducible build artifacts for PyPI, npm, and Go modules with deterministic version metadata and build inputs.
- Integrate artifact signing (in-toto provenance + GPG or sigstore) and store signatures alongside published packages.
- Ensure packaging workflows emit SBOM and provenance metadata (build environment, commit, PR id, builder image digest).
- Update SDK release docs and examples showing how streaming retry semantics map to semantic versioning and migration notes for minor/major bumps.
Acceptance criteria:
1) GitHub Actions workflows (.github/workflows/publish-python.yml, publish-npm.yml, publish-go.yml) successfully build and publish to test registries and include provenance metadata file (provenance.json) and detached signature.
2) Releases include SBOM and in-toto statement referencing build materials; artifacts are reproducible locally using documented steps.
3) SDK client change logs and migration notes mention streaming ergonomics and retry-backoff changes with clear guidance (example code for Python async generator, TS readable stream, Go io.Reader-based stream).
4) A sample end-to-end CI run captured in CI logs and linked here for audits.
Approach / Implementation Notes:
- Reproducible builds: pin builder container digests, use deterministic ./build scripts, set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH where applicable, and normalize tar/zip metadata.
- Provenance: adopt in-toto provenance format; record git commit, PR number, user who triggered release, builder image digest, and list of input artifacts. We will sign statements using sigstore (cosign) where possible; fallback to GPG for PyPI wheels if needed.
- Packaging specifics:
  * Python: build wheels + sdist using build isolated environment, upload to TestPyPI first. Generate provenance.json and .sig; integrate twine upload step that attaches signature.
  * npm: generate tgz with deterministic ordering, produce SBOM via OSS-Licenses tool, publish to npm registry with 2FA stub for publishing user in CI.
  * Go: use goreleaser with reproducible config, push modules to proxy with signed checksums and include provenance metadata in release assets.
- CI safety: release job requires a protected tag and review approval; secret access controlled via ephemeral OIDC tokens.
- Streaming ergonomics + versioning: we will treat API ergonomic changes as minor version bumps if backwards-compatible (e.g., additional overloads), and major if behavior changes (e.g., switching from callback to async iterator). Provide migration examples in README and the changelog.
- Docs & examples: add a dedicated section in the SDK repo: docs/releasing.md and examples/streaming/migration-guide.{py,ts,go}.
Links / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/SDK+Release+Provenance (internal)
- Draft CI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3456 (WIP)
- Example workflow: .github/workflows/publish-python.yml (in PR)
Open questions / trade-offs:
- sigstore vs GPG: cosign provides better integration with OIDC-based ephemeral credentials; some enterprise customers still require GPG signatures for PyPI. Plan: implement cosign as primary and GPG as optional step behind a flag.
- Artifact storage: store provenance + signatures in GitHub release assets vs. an internal artifact store. Initial approach: GitHub release assets for visibility, mirror to internal S3 for long-term retention.
- Reproducibility guarantees: full reproducibility across OSes is hard; we will document supported builder images and provide a reproducibility checklist for contributors.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after SDK team sync. Initial scope includes in-toto provenance and basic cosign integration.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Spiked on cosign + Python wheel signing; created draft GH Actions workflow at https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3456. Found that twine currently does not support cosign by default; planned workaround is to attach signature as release asset and upload wheel normally.

2026-03-12 Dev review: Requested we add SBOM generation step for npm and Go. Also flagged that Go modules require specific goreleaser config to keep checksums stable. Added ENG-11456 as dependency for CI artifact signing primitives.

2026-03-13 QA: Added test matrix to ensure test registry publishes succeed for python 3.9-3.12, node 16-20, go 1.20-1.22. Blocker: corporate npm 2FA policy requires a long-lived machine user until we finish OIDC flow mapping.
